In 1919, Charles Schenck was charged with violating the Espionage Act. The Supreme Court ruled that Schenck's actions created a “clear and present danger.”

How did the decision in this case affect the rights of U.S. citizens?

options.label: A
options.text: By establishing restrictions on the right to vote

options.label: B
options.text: By protecting the freedoms of religious minorities

options.label: C
options.text: By placing limits on freedom of expression

options.label: D
options.text: By protecting the rights of accused persons
